title: Most People Expect AI to Reduce Jobs for Humans
paragraphs: As AI becomes an increasingly common tool, there has been a lot of debate over how it will affect people's lives — and jobs — around the world.

One big question is whether AI will create jobs for humans or reduce them. And surveys done by Pew Research Center earlier this year found that people in 34 out of 37 countries believe that AI is more likely to reduce human jobs than it is to create new ones.

Australians and South Koreans are most likely to believe that AI will result in job losses, with 76% of survey respondents in both countries saying it will lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years. In the US, 71% of respondents have the same opinion.

Of all the countries surveyed, only Nigerians seem slightly more optimistic than pessimistic, with 27% saying AI will lead to more new jobs, compared to 26% saying it will result in fewer jobs. However, 30% also say they aren't sure what effect AI will have.
They aren't alone either. In some countries, many people say they're unsure what AI means for the job market. In the Philippines, 54% say they aren't sure, as do 49% in Thailand and 42% in Kenya.

Outside of just job losses or job creation, the world's feelings about AI use in daily life are mixed. Across all 37 countries surveyed by Pew, an average of 37% of people are more concerned about AI than excited by it — but 41% are both concerned and excited at the same time! Only people in Israel are more excited than concerned.

Globally, people are also more likely to say AI will increase the gap between rich and poor, with 28% saying AI will increase that gap, versus 5% saying AI will shrink it. However, 26% also think it won't make much difference — and 36% aren't sure.
